properties.description: Every presented data beat matches the accepted-input prefix, including zero padding, truncation, order and final-byte marking; comparisons do not require ready.
Every presented status matches the next completed accepted input frame, independently of data-channel progress.
Blocked data and status responses retain validity and payload until acceptance or reset.
Synchronous reset clears both response valids and cancels all queued epoch obligations without clearing historical failures.
Checks source hold behavior, reset-time source validity, bounded frame lengths and meaningful control/payload observations; unknowns cannot establish success.
Combinational final-marker completion checks require no outstanding accepted frame, data, status or presented valid, with a sufficient quiet drain tail; bounded-storage exhaustion remains unresolved.
Every presented data byte must match the accepted input prefix or a justified zero-padding byte; unsolicited data is an alarm, independently of ready.
Every presented data beat has the expected final-byte marker for the clamped 4..8-byte output frame.
Presented status responses match completed accepted input frames in order, including both lengths and padding/truncation flags, independently of data completion.
Data and status remain stable while blocked; synchronous reset clears presented valids and cancels queued obligations without clearing historical alarms.

Checks meaningful observations for unknowns, source reset/blocked-offer protocol, the 1..12-byte input bound, and bounded scoreboard exhaustion. These alarms do not classify invalid inputs as DUT failures.

Combinational final-post completion check: no incomplete input, queued response, or remaining valid; reset is low, both sinks are ready, and at least 32 uninterrupted idle drain edges have occurred. This common minimum does not certify the separately required 128-cycle final-tail qualification.
Presented data beats must match already accepted ordered prefixes, zero padding, truncation at eight bytes, and the required final-byte marker, independently of m_ready.
Presented status responses must correspond in order to completed accepted input frames and contain the exact original length, adjusted length, pad and truncate fields, independently of h_ready.
Blocked data and status responses must retain valid and all enabled payload fields through the following edge unless reset cancels them.
A synchronous reset edge clears both presented response valids and cancels all private outstanding inventories without clearing earlier alarms.
Meaningful accepted input observations and transfer controls must be known; accepted frames and outstanding inventories must remain within the contract and private scoreboard bounds.

Combinational final-marker check requires a qualifying ready-high idle tail of at least 32 edges and complete acceptance and draining of uncancelled input, data and status obligations; no additional clock edge is required.
Every presented data byte is justified by an already accepted input prefix, with zero padding only after a short frame completes.
Presented last markers match known frame boundaries; boundaries not yet established by accepted inputs remain unresolved.
Presented statuses independently follow completed input-frame order and report original length, adjusted length, padding and truncation.
Blocked data and status responses preserve valid and payload until transfer or reset.
Synchronous reset clears both response valids and cancels queued epoch obligations without clearing historical violations.

The final-post marker combinationally checks that input is idle, all accepted frames are complete and both independent response queues are consumed; unknown or exhausted monitor state cannot establish success.
Every presented data beat matches the already accepted byte prefix, including zero padding, truncation, ordering and final-byte marking; checked independently of ready.
Every presented status matches the next completed accepted input frame, with correct original length, adjusted length and padding/truncation flags, independently of data completion.
Blocked data and status presentations retain valid and their complete payload until acceptance or reset.
A synchronous reset edge clears both response valids and cancels the private epoch queues without erasing previously recorded violations.
Accepted-input observations, meaningful handshake controls and bounded scoreboard capacity remain determinate and representable; unknown accepted bytes never establish successful comparisons.
At the final-post marker, combinationally require no incomplete accepted frame, queued data, queued status or remaining source/response valid; no additional clock edge is required.
Every presented data byte is justified by an earlier accepted input prefix or by zero padding after input completion; byte order and truncation are checked regardless of ready.
Every presented data beat has the required last indication at the clamped frame boundary, including streaming partial prefixes.
Presented headers correspond in order to completed accepted frames, with exact original length, adjusted length, padding and truncation flags; header consumption is independent of data consumption.
Blocked data and header responses retain valid and all enabled payload fields through the next observation, unless reset cancels them.

Synchronous reset clears response valids and cancels scoreboard obligations without erasing earlier alarms. Meaningful unknown controls or accepted payloads, oversized frames and scoreboard exhaustion cannot establish success.

Combinational final-marker completion check requires no incomplete input or outstanding data/header obligation, no remaining presented valid or source offer, and at least 32 uninterrupted drain-tail edges. It does not infer unbounded liveness or certify the externally required 128-edge final-tail qualification.
Presented data matches the already accepted input prefix or completion-justified zero padding, independently of sink readiness.

Presented statuses match completed accepted frames in order, with exact lengths and padding/truncation flags; status retirement is independent of data retirement.
Blocked data and status remain valid and stable; synchronous reset clears output valids and cancels outstanding epoch obligations without erasing historical alarms.

Classifies unknown meaningful observations, illegal source reset or blocked-offer behavior, input lengths exceeding twelve bytes, and bounded scoreboard exhaustion as alarms rather than successful DUT checks.

Enabled combinationally at the final-post marker: all accepted input and both response channels must be complete and empty, with no remaining offers or valids and at least 32 ready-high idle drain edges. The evaluator separately qualifies the required 128-cycle final tail; this minimum is not a certification of that qualification.
Presented data must match the already accepted byte prefix in order, with zero padding, eight-byte truncation and correct final-byte marking, independently of ready.

Classifies source hold, reset-time validity, accepted frame-length bounds and meaningful control/payload observations; unknown observations do not establish success.

Checks source hold, reset-time source validity, accepted frame-length bounds and meaningful observations. Unknowns do not establish success; source violations classify invalid input rather than DUT correctness.

The final-post marker combinationally checks completion of the input frame and both independent response queues, with no remaining presented valid. Storage exhaustion or a tail shorter than the development minimum of 32 cycles is unresolved. Final evaluations supply the required 128-cycle tail; no unbounded liveness claim is made.

Checks meaningful control and source observations, source stability while blocked, zero source validity during reset, and the twelve-byte accepted frame bound. Source violations classify invalid inputs, not DUT correctness. Unknown meaningful observations cannot establish success.

Storage exhaustion or fewer than 32 uninterrupted ready-high, reset-low, no-offer tail cycles is unresolved, not successful completion. Final evaluation supplies a 128-cycle tail; this is not an unbounded liveness proof.
